purpose: Structured GAO ledger separating semiconductor program authorization, awards, disbursement, milestones, workforce activity, R&D governance, qualified output, customer delivery, and dependence.

events.geography: United States; semiconductor manufacturing, materials, packaging, workforce, and advanced microelectronics R&D
events.date_precision: GAO-26-109121; reported award, disbursement, milestone, workforce, and governance vintages are retained separately
events.denominator: About $50 billion in semiconductor-related programs; 49 projects across 24 companies; milestone and R&D figures use report-specific denominators and are not one completion rate
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO review, preserving program finance, project, milestone, workforce, governance, and realization stages as separate events
events.missingness: No project-level yield, accepted output, customer delivery, worker retention, local incidence, import substitution, or external-response panel is retained
events.exposure: Commerce oversees about $50 billion, including $39 billion for facilities/equipment incentives and $11 billion for advanced microelectronics R&D; GAO reports active project and governance exposure
events.alternatives_before_action: Projects and institutions may use alternate suppliers, research vehicles, workforce pipelines, private financing, allied coordination, or foreign capacity; project-level alternative availability is not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Awards and disbursements can fund facilities, equipment, research, and workforce activity while cancellation, redesign, delay, local infrastructure needs, and dependence remain possible
events.choice_or_response: By July 2026, 49 projects across 24 companies had been awarded; by April 2026, $13.1 billion had been disbursed; 24 milestones were complete, 125 in progress, and 9 past anticipated dates
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Commerce, awardees, research institutions, workforce partners, suppliers, customers, and state/local hosts control different stages; no actor controls the complete capacity-to-delivery chain
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Commerce disbursed against award and milestone activity; GAO also reports cancellation or revision of about $7.8 billion in advanced-microelectronics R&D awards and insufficiently detailed plans for NSTC, NAPMP, and the Industrial Advisory Committee
events.immediate_outcome: Program commitment, disbursement, milestone activity, workforce funding, and governance transition are visible without being treated as production or autonomy
events.protected_outcome: Qualified domestic production, research capability, skilled-worker retention, supply continuity, and strategic room could be protected if later output, delivery, and alternatives materialize; none is verified here
events.sacrificed_outcome: Delay, duplicated transition costs, local infrastructure burden, workforce attrition, or continued foreign exposure cannot be assigned to a project, worker, customer, or place from this aggregate review
events.cost_risk_transfer: Implementation and dependence risk can shift among public budgets, firms, workers, host communities, customers, and foreign suppliers; distribution is not measured
events.later_outcome: Facility qualification, yield, accepted output, worker hiring and retention, customer delivery, import substitution, supplier switching, alliance coordination, and external response remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: GAO frames governance and R&D implementation as capacity and dependence issues; affected workers, communities, customers, firms, and foreign partners are not interviewed or linked to these program stages
events.public_or_collective_response: Federal oversight and program redesign are observed; downstream firm, worker, local, customer, allied, or adversarial response is not linked
events.counterexample: A project can receive a disbursement after a completed milestone while production remains in qualification; cancellation of one R&D vehicle can also coexist with capability transfer or redesign elsewhere
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-109121; reported program and governance figures are not a causal investment estimate, output measure, or autonomy result

arrows.evidence: GAO reports about $50 billion in semiconductor-related programs and 49 awarded projects across 24 companies
arrows.counterexample: Authorization or award is not an operating facility, qualified output, or reduced import exposure
arrows.remaining_gap: Project-level construction, qualification, ownership, and production records

arrows.evidence: $13.1 billion was disbursed by April 2026; 24 milestones were complete and 125 remained in progress
arrows.counterexample: Payment and milestone completion do not establish yield, accepted output, customer delivery, or worker retention
arrows.remaining_gap: Facility/equipment qualification, output, acceptance, workforce retention, and customer records

arrows.from: R&D governance vehicle and workforce funding
arrows.to: usable domestic research and production capability
arrows.evidence: Four awardees received workforce funding; GAO reports R&D cancellations/revisions and insufficiently detailed governance plans
arrows.counterexample: Training or a governance reset can improve future capability, but neither proves skilled-worker retention, qualified research output, or production continuity
arrows.remaining_gap: Project-year workforce retention, research output, governance execution, facility qualification, and operating yield

arrows.to: customer supply continuity and reduced foreign dependence
arrows.evidence: The reviewed GAO route does not link a named project to accepted product, customer shipment, import displacement, or substitute qualification
arrows.counterexample: Domestic capacity can grow while refined inputs, specialized equipment, customers, or second-source capability remain externally controlled
arrows.remaining_gap: Named project, accepted output, customer delivery, input provenance, supplier switch, and import-exposure change

arrows.to: local incidence, alliance coordination, or geopolitical leverage
arrows.evidence: No same-project record links program realization to worker/community burden, allied behavior, supplier concession, refusal, or state response
arrows.counterexample: Capability may create no leverage if alternatives absorb the shock; public spending may create local burden without strategic benefit
arrows.remaining_gap: Same project/place/customer record with incidence, alternative, switch, negotiation, concession, or external behavior

boundary: This ledger formalizes semiconductor program implementation and governance stages. It does not estimate output, jobs, wages, customer supply, autonomy, or geopolitical leverage.
storage_boundary: No project database, company archive, facility file, or workforce microdata is retained; only bounded GAO findings and explicit open links are represented.
